extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of practical geometry, mensuration, surveying and artisans working with measures (historical/technical audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and rules for constructing and measuring geometric figures (triangles, polygons, solids), for mensuration of volumes (barrels) and for practical balancing/weight procedures used by artisans and surveyors in a historical mathematical treatise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use similarity (simile) to find proportional distances
rubrics_metrics.description: Use similar planes/triangles and projection to locate points at proportional distances and determine corresponding lengths (the text repeatedly invokes similarity: 'simile al piano', 'simili fra ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project lines from one plane to another and compare corresponding segments: form similar triangles between observer and objects (occhio, piano, fineftra) to compute unknown distances; manipulate 'catetto' and 'piano' via these similar constructions to transfer proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding catheti and rectangular-triangle relations via projection
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine lengths of catheti (catetto) in right triangles by constructing rectangular projections and using proportional relations among the sides ('il catetto ... la linea ... tanto quanto ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the rectangular window/plane (fineftra/ponto) as a reference: cut rectangles in the projection, trace the corresponding catheti and apply the proportional relations given (seek 'il catetto sopra' etc.) to deduce unknown sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing regular polygons from squares and known ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct regular figures (square, octagon, equilateral octagon, polygons) by subdividing or extending a square and using arithmetic/ratio rules ('octagono eqiatero ... il quadrato ... la ratioe quadrature').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use side-length multipliers and known proportional formulas (e.g., converting a square into an octagon by specific subdivisions, using k·m multipliers noted in the text) and follow the enumerated arithmetical recipes to build the desired regular polygon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive polygonal side/angle relations by arithmetic scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate the number of sides and side-length via arithmetic series (the manuscript gives many expressions like 'k·m, 2·k·m, ...' showing how to scale to obtain different regular polygons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed multiplicative factors (examples include sequences 'k, m, k·m, ...') and angle-side recipes shown; use the described equal divisions and comparisons of faces to produce polygons with prescribed properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring barrel capacity via sectional counting and grouping (botte/barili)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute how many barrels/pails are filled by counting 'pila', grouping piles, and converting between units (the long section on 'botte', 'barili', 'pila' gives rules for aggregating and converting volumes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the center and use counts of fills and piles ('trouaro centro ... i qunti di ... tratto'); group fills into canonical bundle sizes, apply the stepwise counting rules (how many piles fill one barrel, how many barrels fill larger aggregates) as exemplified in the numerical passages to obtain total volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for counting rotations/piles when filling containers
rubrics_metrics.description: When filling by repeated batches/piles, use the given combinatorial rules to compute totals: how many piles (pile/empiria) correspond to full containers and how to split residuals ('quante pile ... ne voitaranno ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the instructions about grouping piles into sets (examples: 2, 3, 4 piles per grouping), use the illustrated examples to manage carries and remainders, and apply the provided numerical recipes for total counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing a rod (baftone) using helper weights and fulcra (bilico, aiuti)
rubrics_metrics.description: To balance a rod on a fulcrum, place helper small stones/weights at prescribed positions and counts; the text prescribes adding 'aiuti' so that the rod achieves equilibrium ('il baftone in bilico ... metti aiuti ... leuara ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the method of adding incremental helper stones ('aiuti') and removing/adding iron weights to find equilibrium. Place supports at fractional positions (palmi distances) and adjust helper weights until balance; the treatise gives stepwise examples (e.g., add 5, 7, etc. aiuti) to attain equilibrium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using marks/notches (tacche) and measure transference with compasses/feathers
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark distances on rods or staffs with notches and use compasses or calipers ('fede', 'fedo', 'tacca') to transfer and compare lengths precisely ('prendi con le fede ... da luna tacca a altra ...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make regular notches and use them as standard units; the instructions tell how to take a notch-to-notch span with the compasses and replicate it along another rod to obtain consistent measures and to sum them to obtain aggregate weights or lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing and comparing faces/facets of solids (cubes, faces) for mensuration
rubrics_metrics.description: When building solids (cubes, solids of revolution) determine face areas and compare them by halving or subdividing faces ('faccia dco cubo', 'una linea piu de laltra ... la mita').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the given recipes to subdivide faces into halves or other fractions, compare resulting areas numerically following the examples, and use these subdivisions to compute volumes or other derived measures of the solid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for collecting and hauling (fune, trarre) polygonal nets and towing loads
rubrics_metrics.description: When pulling loads or collecting rope bundles, arrange polygons/triangles in sequences and compute the required haul lengths and numbers of turns ('tutta la fune refta ... la parte raccolta in mano per lo tirare').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather successive triangles/quadrilaterals as described, count the number of component squares/triangles (the manuscript gives example counts and the ratios like 900, 520, etc.), and use these counts to calculate the required rope and mechanical advantage for hauling.
